name: Signed Sentence
oneLiner: The people who run your Grant, photographed plainly, and the one signed sentence a month they send you: a category leader's promise on deep linen, forest green and a single ochre accent.
concept:
The buyer is a burnt-out executive director or communications lead who has been told to apply one vendor test: can the agency tell me, in one sentence, what it did to my account last month? Signed Sentence puts that artefact above the fold and, this round, puts the person who wrote it beside it. The hero is a single plate: an eye-level documentary portrait of the account lead (Kristen B., COPD Foundation) sharing top and bottom edges with her August note, mounted in a forest-green frame, signed in ochre ink, with the three ledger figures (CTR against Google's 5% floor, spend of $10k, policy checks 14/14), a 12-month CTR line and the Google endorsement as a rubber stamp hanging off the corner. The sentence is proof; the numbers are context; the face is the reason to believe both.

The ground is re-set so the direction is no longer a cream-and-red sibling of Amplitude. The page is deep linen (#EDE5D5) with lighter oat cards (#F6F1E7); forest green (#1F3D2B) is the second colour and carries the institutional weight: the nav band, the note's frame and mat, the stamp, the eyebrow, the figures. Ochre (#C8912A) is the only accent and is spent on exactly four things: the CTA fill, the italic phrase in every H1, the hand-drawn underline and highlighter marks, and the signature ink. There is no red, vermilion or coral anywhere. Fraunces stays as the display serif at SOFT 12 (bookish, not Cooper); Satoshi is substituted by Instrument Sans from Google Fonts for body and UI, named as such in the spec so the client can decide whether to self-host Satoshi later.

Because the thesis is people, photography is designed in from the start rather than hoped for: every image slot in the mockups is a warm duotone CSS frame (forest shadows to ochre highlight, window light top-left, a soft out-of-focus figure, a fine grain from repeating-linear-gradient) with a real-feeling caption naming a person, a role and a client. The frames are honest about being pre-shoot ('Shoot pending' tag) and the captions are the design contract for the shoot: eye level, natural light, mid-task, named. The register is a leader's relief, calm because it has done this 780 times, with the scale numbers on the same hairline as the note.
distinctFrom: It is the only direction with a second dark colour (forest green bands and frames) rather than a single accent on paper, the only one whose hero object is a photographed person next to something they signed, and the only one with no blue and no red on the page at all.

palette.note: Deeper than the cream of the other directions; the whole page, never #FFFFFF. Reads as unbleached linen next to the forest band.
The note card, badge tiles, form panels. Lifted one step from the ground; 3px radius; a 1px hairline or a green mat, never a drop-shadow-only card.
Warm near-black for headlines, body, figures. 13.9:1 on linen, 6.2:1 as the CTA label on ochre.
Ledes, captions, mono labels, footnotes. 6.0:1 on linen, 6.5:1 on the oat card, so 11px mono captions stay AA.

Nav band, footer band, the note's frame and mat, the stamp, eyebrows, ticker figures, compliant states, the focus ring on linen (9.5:1, clears the 3:1 non-text minimum). 9.5:1 as text on linen; hover #16301F.

The single accent, as fills and marks only: CTA pill (with ink text, 6.2:1), hand-drawn underline, highlighter tint at 42%, signature ink, active nav rule, rotator dot. Never body text on linen (2.2:1).
Ochre for small text and the dashed 5% floor line: 4.9:1 on linen. Display variant #A8761A (3.2:1) is allowed only for the italic H1 phrase at 40px and above.
Ochre for 11px mono text on forest green (mat line, footer labels): 7.3:1. Linen #EDE5D5 on forest is 9.5:1 for nav links.
1px rules for ledgers, ticker, client roll, section dividers; also the inactive eligibility arc. Decorative, no contrast target.

typography.display: Fraunces (Google Fonts), variable: weight 500 for H1/H2, 600 for wordmark, figures and small caps; SOFT axis fixed at 12 (10 on the wordmark), never above 20; opsz 144 on the H1 only, 36 for the note sentence and ledger figures, 24 for wordmark, stamp and client roll. Italic 500 in ochre-display for the emphasised phrase in every H1; italic 400 at opsz 36 for the note sentence.
typography.body: Instrument Sans (Google Fonts) 400/500/600/700, substituting Satoshi, which is Fontshare-only and blocked in the review viewer. Same humanist-grotesk voice and near-identical metrics, so the 780 existing clients see continuity; if leadership prefers Satoshi in production it can be self-hosted as WOFF2 under the ITF Free Font Licence with no layout change.
typography.mono: JetBrains Mono (Google Fonts) 400/500: eyebrows, dates, ledger units, stamp text, mat line, captions, the CTA time tag, the status ticker. Tabular numerals on by default.
typography.scaleNotes: H1 58px / 1.04 / -0.025em at 1200 (two lines: 'You run the mission.' holds one line in the 528px column), 40px on phones. H2 44px / 1.08. H3 26px / 1.2. Note sentence Fraunces italic 20.5px / 1.3 (19.5px on phones). Body 17px / 1.5, lede 17-18px. Mono labels 11-12px uppercase (the desktop eyebrow 11.5px so it holds one line in the 528px column), tracking 0.02-0.09em depending on room; nothing below 11px anywhere. Ledger and ticker figures Fraunces 600 at 20-24px with 11px mono units. Client roll set in five typographic voices (mono tracked caps, Fraunces small caps, Instrument Sans 700 tracked caps, Fraunces italic, Fraunces 600) between hairlines. Radii: 3px for paper objects and tiles, 5px for the green frame, 999px for pills; nothing else. Spacing on an 8px base; nav 72px (60 on phones); 56px gutters at 1200, 16px on phones.

layout:
- 01 Nav: a 72px forest-green band (the one dark surface above the fold). Mark in linen with an ochre bell arc, Fraunces wordmark 'Nonprofit Megaphone' (italic second word). Links in linen: Ad Grant management (active, ochre rule), Services, Results, Team, Pricing, Blog. Right: 'Client reports' with a lock glyph, ochre pill 'Book a free call'. Sticky after 200px.
- 02 Hero (528 / 512 split, 48px gap, 44px top padding). Left: forest mono eyebrow 'One of nine inaugural Google-certified Ad Grant agencies · 2019'; H1 'You run the mission. We'll run the Grant.' with the italic ochre phrase and the drawn underline; 17px lede carrying 780+ and $48M+ in ink; ochre pill 'Book a free call · 30 MIN' and the text link 'Am I eligible? · 2 MIN'; mono fine print (flat monthly fee, no % of spend, 100% grant-acquisition guarantee); a hairline; then the guarantee block with Amber Snow's small duotone frame, 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy.' and a direct 'Email Amber directly' link (her address is not printed in the mockup; confirm it with the client before build). Right: the plate. A 296 x 476 duotone portrait of the account lead and the 380px signed note share the same top and bottom edge and overlap by 164px; the note is a forest frame with an oat card inside (header 'Your month, in one sentence · No. 14', the sentence with two ochre highlights, the three-figure ledger, the 12-month CTR line against the dashed 5% floor with source and date, the ochre signature, name, client and month) and the stamp 'Recommended by Google's first Head of Ad Grants' hanging off the bottom-right corner of the frame, over nothing; the mat line above the card, like a folder tab, reads 'Client-approved · replies in 1 day · 1 of 3' with the rotator dots. One caption runs under the whole plate: 'Kristen B., account lead for COPD Foundation. Portland office, mid-call; natural light, eye level; her August sentence, right, exactly as the client received it.'
- 03 Trust strip (two hairline rows). Row one: 780+ nonprofits, $48M+ Grant managed, 100% acquisition, 60+ on staff in forest Fraunces with mono units and 'as of Sep 2026', then the Google Partner tile (green-bordered oat tile, per Google's badge rules) and Inc. 5000 x4. Row two: the typographic client roll UNCF, Scouting America, COPD Foundation, YWCA Chicago, Earthwatch, Solar Sister, AAU, JFCS.
- 04 'Three ways nonprofits lose the Grant': a rules table (requirement / what Google does if you miss it, in policy language / what we do about it), followed by the page's one data object, a real named account's 12-month CTR line against the dashed floor, with source and date.
- 05 'Who's on your account' (full width, on linen): the first photography section. Eight to twelve documentary duotone-graded portraits of account leads in a 4-column contact-sheet grid, each with name, role and 'Nonprofits I support' mono caption; hover reveals a second candid frame. Until the shoot, this ships as a typographic roster, never stock.
- 06 'A month with us' (5/7): Week 1 to Week 4 as numbered paragraphs on the left; on the right the actual reporting email with mono REDACTED tags over client data, and the note format repeated at small size, so the artefact on the site is literally what you receive.
- 07 Results as a hairline ledger (Organization / Vertical / What we changed / Outcome / Period), each row expanding to a case sheet with the fixed KPI trio and a 'Forward to board' PDF action; consented beneficiary photography lives inside the expanded sheet only.
- 08 'The guarantee, in Amber's words' (forest-green band, linen text): Amber Snow's portrait frame at 5 columns, the $25 clause set as fine print with a signature line, her email in plain text, the 100% grant-acquisition promise stated with its conditions. This band is the page's second green surface, pairing with the nav.
- 09 Services as a hairline ledger (seven rows) with a fee-range column ('flat monthly fee · no % of spend') and a 'Good fit if / Not a fit if' column; the fit column survives if pricing is refused.
- 10 Eligibility checker: an oat panel with four questions; one forest arc completes per answer; end states include the honest 'You're not eligible, here's why' card for hospitals, schools and government entities.
- 11 Closing CTA on linen: 'Thirty minutes, no deck.' Ochre pill, eligibility link, the guarantee line repeated with Amber's frame.
- 12 Footer: forest-green band with linen text and ochre-light labels; four columns (services, company incl. Team, Pricing, Blog, Client reports; resources; contact with the CEO's email), Google Partner tile, Certified Professional wordmark, Inc. 5000 x4, a linen newsletter input.
imagery:
Photography is the direction's largest budget line and its thesis, so the mockups design for it instead of waiting for it. Every image slot is a warm duotone CSS frame: a 162-degree gradient from sage (#3C5C41) through forest (#1F3D2B) into a dark ochre (#5A4A22), a soft radial ochre highlight and a blurred linen 'window light' block top-left, an out-of-focus figure drawn as two blurred SVG shapes, a 1px repeating-linear-gradient grain at 5-7% blended overlay, and an inset vignette. Each frame carries a mono 'Shoot pending' tag and a real caption: name, role, client, place and the shooting instruction (natural light, eye level, mid-task). Desktop shows two such frames (the 296 x 476 account-lead portrait in the plate, Amber Snow's 64 x 78 frame in the guarantee block); the phone shows a 358 x 212 landscape crop of the lead and Amber's 54 x 66 frame. The captions double as the shoot brief.

The real shoot: two days, at least 20 staff, in Chicago and Portland, natural window light, eye level, working (on a call, at the Ads console), warm-neutral wardrobe, no coloured backdrops; delivered as colour but graded with a warm curve so they sit on linen, and offered in the duotone as a hover state only. Beneficiary imagery from six flagship clients (COPD screenings, Solar Sister entrepreneurs, Scouting America troops, Earthwatch field teams) is sourced with written consent, dignity-first, never reaching hands or coins. Proof objects carry trust: real reporting emails with labelled mono REDACTED tags (a labelled redaction reads as honesty; a blur reads as hiding), the real 5% CTR line from a client account, the note format identical on site and in the inbox. Illustration is limited to one hand-drawn ochre set of about 20 marks (underline, circled numbers, arrows, marginalia) and the forest eligibility arcs; no character illustration, no icons in marketing pages beyond a 1.5px line set for UI.
motion: Quiet, brief, and off by default under prefers-reduced-motion. Reveals use a 2kB IntersectionObserver (or GSAP ScrollTrigger, free in Webflow): opacity 0 to 1 with a 12px rise, 500ms ease-out, once. Hero on load, 900ms total then stillness: headline words settle with a 40ms stagger; the ochre underline draws left to right via stroke-dashoffset over 600ms after the headline lands; the portrait fades up, then the note rises 8px and settles, then the stamp thumps in (scale 1.12 to 1, 220ms, opacity only). Hover: the CTA darkens to #B8811F; the note's shadow lengthens 4px with no tilt; portrait frames crossfade from the duotone grade to the colour frame of the same person; every figure shows a source-and-date tooltip. The note rotates through three approved client sentences on a 7-second crossfade, pausable via the mat dots. The eligibility checker completes one forest arc per answer (300ms). Section hairlines extend 0 to 100% as they enter. No parallax, cursor followers, kinetic type, WebGL or smooth-scroll library. Under prefers-reduced-motion everything renders in its final state and the rotator stops.
mobile: The 390px hero is a designed state, not a squeeze. Nav is a 60px forest band: mark and wordmark, a 36px ochre 'Book a call' pill and a 44px menu target. Then, in order: the eyebrow on two mono lines; the H1 at 40px holding two lines ('You run the mission.' / 'We'll run the Grant.' with the italic ochre phrase and underline intact); the 17px lede; a full-width 52px ochre CTA with the 30 MIN tag (y = 371); the centred 'Am I eligible? · 2 MIN' link with a 44px target (y = 435); mono fine print; and the guarantee line with Amber's small frame, all above a 760px fold. Below the fold the plate stacks: the landscape duotone frame of the account lead (358 x 212, 'Shoot pending' tag, full caption), then the note in its green frame at full width with the same sentence, the 3-column ledger, the CTR line, the signature, and the stamp converted to an inline bordered forest chip beneath the signature (no rotation, no overhang); the mat line above the card keeps the rotator dots. One trust element follows: 780+ / $48M+ / 60+ in three hairline columns, the Google Partner tile and the Michelle Hurtado quote. Key sections below: the rules table becomes stacked requirement cards with the three columns as labelled rows; the contact sheet goes to two columns; ledgers become two-line rows; the eligibility checker is one question per screen. Targets 44px minimum, focus ring 3px forest on linen and linen on green.
a11y: WCAG 2.2 AA is the acceptance target on every element, measured on its actual background: ink on linen 13.9:1; muted on linen 6.0:1 and on oat card 6.5:1 (so the 11px mono captions and labels pass with margin); forest on linen 9.5:1; linen on forest 9.5:1; ochre-light on forest 7.3:1; ink on the ochre CTA 6.2:1; ochre-ink #86590E for small ochre text 4.9:1; the ochre-display italic #A8761A is restricted to the H1 at 40px+ where 3.2:1 clears the large-text threshold; raw ochre #C8912A is never used as text. Minimum text size 11px (mono labels), body 17px. Focus: a visible 3px forest-green outline with 3px offset on linen (9.5:1, clears WCAG 2.2 non-text contrast; raw ochre would be 2.2:1 and fail), switched to linen on the green band; every link and button has one. Targets 44px+ on phones, 40px+ nav pills on desktop. Motion is gated behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; the rotator stops and reveals render final under reduced motion. Text equivalents: decorative SVG (mark, underline, signature, arcs, silhouettes, grain) is aria-hidden; the CTR sparkline carries role=img with a sentence describing the 12-month rise above the 5% floor; the stamp carries role=img with its wording; every duotone frame is a figure with a figcaption naming the person and role; ledger figures pair a unit with each number; the note's three figures repeat what the sentence says in prose so nothing depends on the highlight colour. Headings are a single H1 then H2s per section; nav is a labelled landmark.

heroCopy.eyebrow: One of nine inaugural Google-certified Ad Grant agencies · 2019
heroCopy.headline: You run the mission. We'll run the Grant.
heroCopy.sub: 780+ nonprofits hand us their $10,000-a-month Google Ad Grant so a named person keeps it compliant, spent well and pointed at the people who need them. $48M+ managed so far. Every month, one sentence on what changed, signed by the lead who did it.

signatureMoments: The plate: an eye-level duotone portrait of the account lead and her signed monthly note sharing the same top and bottom edge, overlapping by 164px, with one caption under both. The person and the sentence are one object; the client sees who wrote it before reading it.

The forest-framed note: an oat card mounted in a #1F3D2B frame with a mat line above the card ('Client-approved · replies in 1 day · 1 of 3'), the sentence with ochre highlights, the three-figure ledger, the CTR line against the dashed 5% floor, and an ochre-ink signature; the Google endorsement is a rubber stamp hanging off the bottom-right corner, an inline chip on phones.

Warm duotone photography as a system: forest shadows, ochre highlights, window light, fine grain, captioned with name, role, client and place; the CSS placeholder frames in the pitch are honest ('Shoot pending') and their captions are the brief for the two-day shoot.
'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy.' pinned under the primary CTA with Amber Snow's small frame and a direct email link; repeated later as a full green band in her words.
Ochre spent four ways only: CTA fill, the italic H1 phrase, the drawn underline and highlighter marks, the signature ink. The discipline is what keeps linen-and-green from tipping into stationery.
dependencies: Fund and schedule the photography before build: a two-day documentary shoot of at least 20 staff (Chicago and Portland), natural light, eye level, working; plus written consent for beneficiary imagery from six flagship clients. Without it the people sections ship as typographic rosters and the direction is materially weaker.
Name the account leads publicly: the hero, the contact sheet and the note all rely on real first names, roles and portraits of staff who are willing to be the face of an account.

Confirm the CEO's public contact address and the 'Inc. 5000 x4' claim with the client before build: neither is in the verified fact list, so the mockups use an 'Email Amber directly' link and the Inc. tile is marked for verification.

Consent for a real statement: three client-approved monthly sentences with figures, client name and month, replacing the illustrative COPD Foundation note in the mockup (its sentence, 11.2% CTR, 9,640 USD, 14/14 and 312 people are placeholders and must not go live).

The operations SLA behind the note: a HubSpot report template, a process owner per account, a Webflow CMS collection (lead, portrait, client, month, sentence, approved flag) and a fallback state ('Report sent 2 Sep'), so the hero is never a lie.
Publish pricing: a fee range and the 'good fit / not a fit' column in the services ledger; if refused, the fit column and the eligibility checker remain as the board-forwardable exits.

Brand decision on the mark: this direction renders the megaphone mark in linen on green and drops brand blue from the page; leadership must approve recolouring the mark (or keep #0A23A2 in the mark only, which the direction tolerates) and confirm Google Partner badge placement on an oat tile meets Google's badge rules.
Font decision: accept Instrument Sans as the body face (Google Fonts, used in the mockups) or fund self-hosting Satoshi as WOFF2 under the ITF Free Font Licence.
A small motion sprint (IntersectionObserver reveals, underline draw, stamp thump, note rotator) or accept the static state, which is fully designed.
risks: The note is an operations promise: an invented or stale sentence is the one thing this buyer punishes. Mitigated by the CMS collection, owner-per-account and fallback state above, and by copy that says 'every monthly report', not a fixed weekday.

Photography that slips leaves the plate half-empty. The duotone frames are honest placeholders for the pitch, not for launch; every photo-led section has a typographic fallback (roster, ledger, labelled screenshots), and the hero can ship as note-only at 380px centred until the portrait exists.

Linen, green and a hand-drawn underline can decay into stationery in an editor's hands. Guardrails are tokens in the Webflow style guide: ochre in four uses only, one green band above the fold and one below, three paper devices per page (note, stamp, underline), Fraunces SOFT never above 20, 11px floor, 3px/5px/pill radii only.

Dropping blue is a real equity change for 780 clients and Google's partner directory. Mitigation: the mark keeps its geometry, the Google Partner badge keeps its own rules, and the change is announced as a sharpening with old and new lockups side by side.

Ochre is a low-contrast hue: the direction depends on the three-tier ochre rule (fill #C8912A, display #A8761A at 40px+, ink #86590E for small text). A build that uses raw ochre for links or captions fails AA immediately; the token sheet names the three and the style guide shows the failing case.

Two dark green surfaces plus duotone frames make the page heavier than the other directions; if the client wants the lightest possible register, keep the nav band and drop the guarantee band to a hairline section.
references: Patagonia Worn Wear and Patagonia Stories: documentary portraits of real people at work, matter-of-fact captions, no stock
Aesop: unbleached neutrals, a single dark green as a second colour, typographic restraint as authority
Anthropic (anthropic.com): warm ground, serif-led editorial calm, one accent used sparingly
Wealthsimple: financial trust delivered with warmth, oversized serif headlines, real people photographed plainly
The New Yorker and Monocle contributor pages: name, role and place under every portrait; the caption as a trust device
Stripe annual letters and Stripe Press: ledgers, hairlines, footnoted and dated figures
37signals / Basecamp: guarantees stated plainly, named humans over logo walls
Duotone editorial photography (Spotify 2015 identity, The Guardian Weekend covers): a two-colour grade that makes a mixed set of portraits read as one system
